title: umami-rich molten slovakian beef dumplings
description: a hearty, comforting dish featuring a rich beef broth and a tender, cheesy filling enclosed in a crispy, fermented dough.
instructions: in a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, yeast, and salt.
gradually add the warm water to the dry ingredients and mix until a shaggy dough forms.
add the butter, onion, and beef broth to the dough and mix until the dough comes together in a sticky ball.
knead the dough for 10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
place the dough in a greased bowl, cover it with plastic wrap, and let it ferment in a warm place for 1 hour.
while the dough is fermenting, cook the ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it's browned, breaking it up into small pieces as it cooks.
add the chopped parsley and grated cheddar cheese to the skillet and stir to combine.
divide the fermented dough into 12 equal pieces and roll each piece into a ball.
flatten each ball of dough into a disk using a rolling pin or your hands.
place a tablespoon of the beef and cheese mixture in the center of each disk, leaving a 1/2-inch border around the edges.
fold the dough over the filling to form a half-moon shape and press the edges together to seal the dumpling.
place the dumplings on a wooden board or a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
dot the tops of the dumplings with the beaten eggs and sprinkle with kosher salt.
bake the dumplings in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until they're golden brown and crispy on the bottom.
serve the dumplings hot, with additional beef broth for dipping if desired.
